title: Proxy trust and single bootstrap fixes
lead: Fix two bugs in shipped code: forwarded headers from an IPv4 proxy on a dual-stack socket, and a bootstrap pairing link that stays valid when several processes start.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the container, the WSGI server and its worker count (S28); the scheduler (S64); any other change to the pairing flow of ADR 0010.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Two notes on S28 describe bugs that already ship.
- `_is_trusted` in `src/larder/web/__init__.py` tests `address in network`. A dual-stack socket reports an IPv4 proxy as `::ffff:10.1.2.3`, an `IPv6Address` that is not in an `IPv4Network`, so forwarded headers are ignored (fail closed) and `Secure` cookies never turn on (`request.scheme` stays `http` in `auth_views._SessionInterface` and `_set_device_cookie`).
- `create_app` calls `auth.ensure_bootstrap` in every process that starts. Each one deletes the unused bootstrap token and logs a new link, so with several workers only the last link works, and a respawn replaces a link an admin is about to use. `tests/test_auth.py::BootstrapTest.test_bootstrap_link_logged_single_use_and_replaced_on_restart` pins the replace-on-start behavior, which stays right for one process.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body: Confirm the bootstrap fix (recommended): `create_app(settings, *, bootstrap=True)`. The dev server and the tests keep the default. A WSGI entrypoint passes `bootstrap=False`, and a new `python -m larder bootstrap` step runs once before the server and logs the one link. Starting a second process never replaces it. ADR 0010 says "each restart replaces it"; the amended wording is "each run of the bootstrap step replaces it". An accepted ADR changes only with the owner's approval.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/larder/web/__init__.py` (`_is_trusted`, `create_app`)
- `src/larder/__main__.py` (`bootstrap` subcommand beside `pair`)
- `tests/test_web_shell.py` (`ProxyHeadersTest`, `AppFactoryTest`)
- `tests/test_auth.py` (`BootstrapTest`)
- `docs/decisions/0010-device-cookie-auth.md` (one sentence, with the owner's approval)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_proxy_headers_applied_from_ipv4_mapped_peer` (`trusted_proxies = ["10.0.0.0/8"]`, peer `::ffff:10.1.2.3`)
2. `test_ipv4_mapped_peer_outside_the_trusted_network_is_ignored` (peer `::ffff:192.0.2.7`)
3. `test_plain_ipv6_peer_in_a_trusted_ipv6_network_is_still_trusted`
4. `test_create_app_without_bootstrap_logs_no_link_and_keeps_the_existing_one` (`assertNoLogs("larder.auth")`; the earlier `/pair/<token>` still answers 200)
5. `test_bootstrap_command_logs_a_working_link_and_replaces_the_previous_one`
6. `test_bootstrap_command_logs_nothing_when_an_admin_device_exists`
7. `test_default_create_app_still_logs_and_replaces_on_start` (the existing behavior, kept)

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. `_is_trusted`: after `ipaddress.ip_address`, build the candidates: the address, plus `address.ipv4_mapped` when it is an `IPv6Address` with one. Trust the peer when any candidate is in any network. Keep both so a `::/0` entry still matches mapped peers.
2. `create_app(settings, *, bootstrap: bool = True)`; call `auth.ensure_bootstrap` only when `bootstrap` is true. Update the docstring.
3. `python -m larder bootstrap`: `auth.require_admin`, `ensure_data_dirs`, connect, `db.migrate`, `auth.sync_people`, `auth.ensure_bootstrap`; return 0, and 2 with a message on `ConfigError`/`DatabaseError` like the other commands. The link is logged by `ensure_bootstrap` as today.
4. With the owner's approval, amend the ADR 0010 sentence about restarts.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Tests and `ruff check .` pass.
- Start two `create_app(settings, bootstrap=False)` apps against one data directory after one `python -m larder bootstrap`: the logged link still works.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
